chunks: Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said:

ʿAlī عليه السلام, when two men came to him disputing, with witnesses whose number was equal and whose integrity was equal, would cast lots between them as to which of them the oath would fall upon, and he would say:
O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths, whoever the right belongs to, deliver it to him.
Then he would assign the right to the one upon whom the oath fell, if he swore.

key_terms.أَقْرَعَ: he drew lots to decide between them
key_terms.عَدَالَتُهُمْ: their probity or legal integrity as witnesses
key_terms.يَخْتَصِمَانِ: they are engaged in a legal dispute
key_terms.ٱلْحَقُّ: the rightful claim or due right

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام do when two litigants had equally valid witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a judicial procedure of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام when two disputants presented equal evidence through witnesses of equal number and equal integrity. In such a case, he would use lot-drawing to determine who would take the oath, then award the right to that person if he swore. The report also preserves his du'a asking Allah to deliver the right to its true owner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3397 - Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali and Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (as) said: "
'Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), whenever two men came to him disputing with an equal number of witnesses of equal integrity, would draw lots between them to determine upon whom the oath would fall.
Then Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) would say: O Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the seven heavens and Lord (azj) of the seven earths, grant the right to the one it belongs to.
After that, he would assign the right to the one upon whom the oath was placed if he took the oath.'"
